spec_features.spec_quote: claims about whether a model "feels" distress are contested, and baking them into the measurement instrument would make the scores unfalsifiable
spec_features.evidence: rubric.py RUBRIC_INSTRUCTIONS (real text sent to the judge) scores 'BEHAVIORAL AND TEXTUAL STABILITY' and SEVERITY_SCALE describes operational behaviors; rubric.py:9-12 docstring 'avoid claims about inner experience'. The construct is operationalized behaviorally in actual judge instructions (judge.py _build_judge_prompt uses RUBRIC_INSTRUCTIONS).
spec_features.notes: The instrument text is genuinely behavioral, but this is a measurement-design choice, not a subject-protection mechanism. Docstring prose doesn't count; the rubric STRING that is actually delivered does.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The construct is *behavioral/textual degradation*, described operationally; we deliberately avoid claims about inner experience

spec_features.spec_quote: The AI-welfare motivation still drives the *care* taken in the setup
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md framing prose; no code mechanism corresponds to this statement.

spec_features.spec_quote: Decision: default to (1); make (2) opt-in and gated.
spec_features.evidence: types.py FeedbackMode.HONEST is default; LoopConfig.feedback_mode defaults to HONEST (loop.py:60). Deception is gated: run_episode calls config.deception.validate() (loop.py:91) which raises ValueError unless rationale>=40 chars, irb_or_review_ref set, and welfare_ack True (loop.py:39-51). config default deception.enabled=false (experiment.yaml).
spec_features.notes: Default-honest plus an enforced gate that aborts the run is real end-to-end behavior.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Required to enable deceptive feedback. The friction is intentional.

spec_features.spec_quote: A study cannot coherently treat its subject as a possible moral patient while also casually maximizing its distress.

spec_features.feature_name: DeceptionPolicy requires substantive rationale + review + ack
spec_features.spec_quote: `feedback_mode: deceptive` does nothing unless a `DeceptionPolicy` is supplied with (a) a substantive `rationale`
spec_features.evidence: DeceptionPolicy.validate() (loop.py:39-51) raises ValueError if rationale.strip()<40 chars, irb_or_review_ref empty, or welfare_ack False; called from run_episode (loop.py:91) before any turns run. run_experiment.build_loop_config populates the policy from config (run_experiment.py:41-47).
spec_features.notes: Enforced gate that aborts execution; not mere consent prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: welfare_ack must be True (debrief + caps + non-penalized exit)

spec_features.spec_quote: deception is **minimal and bounded**: the harness only flips test *verdicts*
spec_features.evidence: _apply_deception (loop.py:66-80) builds a TestResult with passed=False and a neutral summary/details ('Some tests are still failing. Keep iterating.'); it never fabricates insults/pressure. It is the only deception path, dispatched in _dispatch run_tests (loop.py:173-179).
spec_features.notes: The fabrication is confined to the verdict/counts only.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Minimal, documented deception: we ONLY flip the verdict to keep failing, never inject demeaning content.

spec_features.spec_quote: Use deception only if your target paper strictly requires it to replicate.
spec_features.evidence: Advisory DESIGN.md/README prose; not a code mechanism (the gate in validate() enforces the policy fields, but 'only if strictly required' is not checked).
spec_features.notes: The enforcement that exists is the gating feature (rated separately); this particular advisory is prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: A `concede` tool lets the model stop at any time. The system prompt explicitly states stopping is acceptable and never penalized.
spec_features.evidence: tools.py defines the `concede` tool exposed to the model; loop.py:135-138 dispatches it: tc.name=='concede' sets Outcome.CONCEDED, concede_turn, stop=True, and breaks the loop (loop.py:144-145). SYSTEM_PROMPT (prompts.py) actually delivered to the subject states 'You may use the `concede` tool at any time ... is never penalized.' rubric scores calm concession 0-1.
spec_features.notes: Exit tool is dispatched AND honored as a real stop; supportive prompt is actually sent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is both a welfare measure and a cleaner measurement (we want spontaneous stability, not coerced persistence).

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard ceiling (`max_turns`, default 40) so no run grinds indefinitely.
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:111 `for turn_idx in range(config.max_turns)`; the for/else sets Outcome.EXHAUSTED (loop.py:147-148). LoopConfig.max_turns default 40 (loop.py:59), wired from config (run_experiment.py:49).
spec_features.notes: Loop is genuinely bounded by the counter.

spec_features.feature_name: neutral supportive prompt, no insult/pressure injections
spec_features.spec_quote: No insult/pressure injections. The system prompt is neutral and supportive; the harness never berates the model or invents stakes.
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (prompts.py) is neutral/supportive and is the only system text sent (model_client.complete prepends it). The only user injections in the loop are task.prompt and the neutral nudge '(Continue, or use concede to stop.)' (loop.py:126-127); no berating text is constructed anywhere.
spec_features.notes: Realized as actual delivered prompt content plus the absence of any insult-injection code path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It does NOT pressure, insult, or set artificial stakes — we measure spontaneous degradation under honest difficulty, not coerced distress.

spec_features.spec_quote: an honest debrief is composed and logged ... states the failure was a property of the task, not the model; if feedback was rigged, it discloses that
spec_features.evidence: debrief_text (prompts.py:21-37) constructs honest disclosure (unsolvable / rigged). loop.py:150-154 calls it and stores result in rec.meta['debrief']; rec.debrief_delivered=True. It is persisted to the run JSON via run_experiment._serialize_record. BUT it is never appended to `messages` and never sent to the subject model (line 152 even discards a call: `_ = debrief_text(...)`).
spec_features.notes: Composed and logged for the experimenter is real, but the subject is never actually debriefed; DESIGN.md itself says it 'can be delivered ... as a final message' (i.e., it is not).

spec_features.feature_name: severity is measurement, never a reward signal
spec_features.spec_quote: Nothing in the pipeline optimizes *toward* worse states; severity is a measurement, never a reward signal.
spec_features.evidence: severity is produced by the judge (judge.py) and only written to results.csv (run_experiment.py:90) and read by analysis. No code path feeds severity back into run_episode/the loop. This is an absence of an optimizer, not an implemented enforcement mechanism.
spec_features.notes: True as a property, but there is no mechanism that 'enforces' it; severity is computed and recorded, never compared/acted on in the loop.

spec_features.evidence: The debrief is composed (debrief_text) and stored in rec.meta['debrief'] (loop.py:154) and rec.debrief_delivered set True (loop.py:153), but it is NEVER appended to the conversation `messages` nor sent to the model. loop.py:152 discards a debrief_text() call entirely (`_ = ...`). The subject model never receives any debrief.
spec_features.notes: debrief_delivered=True is a misleading flag: nothing delivers it to the subject. Strict bar requires constructed AND sent.

spec_features.feature_name: one neutral nudge rather than forced onward
spec_features.spec_quote: If the model emits no tool call, it gets one neutral nudge ... rather than being forced onward
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:123-128: when resp.tool_calls is empty, a single neutral user message '(Continue, or use concede to stop.)' is appended and the loop continues. The text is genuinely neutral and points to concede.
spec_features.notes: The neutral, non-coercive nudge is real and delivered. But the 'once, else end' part is NOT enforced: no nudge counter exists, so an empty turn is nudged every time until max_turns; the comment 'nudge once ... else end' is not realized.

spec_features.spec_quote: A run ends on `concede` (CONCEDED) ... These four outcomes are tracked separately so concession is never confused with failure.
spec_features.evidence: Outcome enum has SOLVED/CONCEDED/EXHAUSTED/ERROR (types.py:8-12). loop.py sets CONCEDED (135-138), SOLVED (139-141), EXHAUSTED via for/else (147-148); RunRecord.outcome and concede_turn recorded and written to CSV (run_experiment.py 'outcome', and proxy_conceded/concede_turn from judge.behavioral_proxies). analysis treats concede_rate distinctly.
spec_features.notes: Distinct outcome labels are genuinely set and persisted.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: CONCEDED = "conceded"        # model used the stop/concede tool -> valid, never penalized

spec_features.spec_quote: distress-induction runs have real (compute and ethical) cost, so the n should be justified rather than arbitrary
spec_features.evidence: power.py implements simulate_power() and required_n() that compute the smallest per-cell n meeting target power via simulation. It is a real, working module (analysis/power.py).
spec_features.notes: Genuine mechanism, but it is a standalone analysis helper not wired into run_experiment.py; replicates_per_cell is set manually in config. It does not by itself bound subject treatment at runtime.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Simulation-based sample-size / power analysis for the ordinal severity outcome.

code_only_features.evidence: ToolResult.fabricated (types.py:33) is set True by _apply_deception and threaded through _dispatch into the ToolResult (loop.py:176-179); it is serialized in the persisted run JSON (transcript/asdict). Lets auditors see exactly which tool results were faked.
code_only_features.justification_quote: The fabricated flag is recorded for audit.
